title: Critical Rendering Path
objective: Explain the steps browsers take to convert HTML/CSS into rendered pixels, and identify which steps a given code change affects.

content_blocks.heading: Overview
content_blocks.body: The critical rendering path is the sequence of steps a browser takes to convert HTML, CSS, and JavaScript into pixels on screen.

content_blocks.heading: The Six Steps
content_blocks.body:
1) Parse HTML into the DOM.
2) Parse CSS into the CSSOM.
3) Combine DOM + CSSOM into the render tree (visible nodes only).
4) Layout: compute the size and position of every render tree node.
5) Paint: fill in pixels for text, color, images, borders, shadows.
6) Composite: combine painted layers in the correct order, using the GPU where possible.

content_blocks.heading: Why This Matters for Performance
content_blocks.body: Changes that only affect paint (e.g. background-color) are cheaper than changes that trigger layout (e.g. width, font-size), because layout invalidates everything downstream of it. CSS properties like `transform` and `opacity` can be composited without touching layout or paint, which is why animating them is preferred for smooth 60fps animations.

exercises.prompt: You change a button's `background-color` on hover. Which critical-rendering-path step is the most expensive one this change triggers?

options: Paint only, for the button's pixels
CSSOM re-parse of the entire stylesheet
definition.explanation: background-color doesn't change any element's size or position, so layout is skipped entirely; the browser only has to repaint the button's own pixels.
